name: Tourist visa (TR)
summary: The standard tourist visa you apply for online through the official Thai e-Visa system before you travel. The single-entry TR lets you stay up to 60 days, plus one 30-day extension at immigration, so up to 90 days in total. Since visa-free stays dropped to 30 days in September 2026, it is the simplest way to get two or three months. The multiple-entry tourist visa (METV) still exists at many embassies: valid 6 months, with up to 60 days per entry.
seoTitle: Thailand tourist visa (TR) 2026: 60 days + 30, e-Visa fee, METV
seoDescription: How to get a Thailand tourist visa through the e-Visa system: 60-day stay, 30-day extension, fees by embassy, 20,000 THB funds, documents, the METV and common mistakes.
validity: Single entry (TR): valid 3 months from issue, so you must enter within that time. Each entry allows up to 60 days. METV: valid 6 months, unlimited entries, up to 60 days per entry.
extendableDetail: Once in Thailand you can extend each 60-day stay by up to 30 days at an immigration office (form TM.7, 1,900 THB), at the officer's discretion. With a METV you can also leave and re-enter before the visa expires for a fresh 60-day stay.
feeNote: The base fee is 1,000 THB for a single entry and 5,000 THB for a METV, but you pay in the local currency of the embassy that handles your e-Visa, for example USD 40 / USD 200 in the US, GBP 30 in the UK and NOK 400 / NOK 2,000 in Norway. Fees are non-refundable.
financialRequirement: Show at least 20,000 THB per person or 40,000 THB per family. Some embassies ask for a current balance only; others (for example Washington) want 3 months of statements. The METV asks for more financial evidence (and often proof of employment or income); the amount is set by each embassy, so check its page.
processingTime: Varies by embassy. Many say to allow up to 14 working days, and the Washington embassy advises applying at least 30 days before departure. Don't apply more than 3 months ahead, because the visa's validity starts on the day it is issued.
keyRequirements: Apply online at thaievisa.go.th before you travel, through the embassy that covers the country where you live
Passport valid for at least 6 months with two blank pages
Proof of funds of at least 20,000 THB per person (40,000 THB per family)
Onward or return flight booking and accommodation for your stay
Tourism, family visits or medical treatment only; no work of any kind
Submit the TDAC within 3 days before each arrival
documents: Recent passport-style photo taken within the last 6 months
Flight booking to Thailand (and out, or onward)
Hotel bookings or an invitation letter with your Thai address
Recent bank statement in your name showing at least 20,000 THB equivalent
Proof of residence in the country where you apply (e.g. residence card, visa or utility bill) if you are not a citizen
For minors: birth certificate and parents' consent letter
For METV: proof of employment or income as required by your embassy

howToApply.detail: On thaievisa.go.th, choose the country where you live. The e-Visa is handled by the Thai embassy or consulate responsible for that country.

howToApply.step: Create an account and choose the visa
howToApply.detail: Select 'Tourist Visa' and then single entry or multiple entry (METV), depending on what your embassy offers.
Upload clear PDFs or JPGs of your passport, photo, bookings and bank statement. Blurry or cropped files are the most common reason for delays.
Pay online in local currency. Some embassies only start processing after payment clears.
You'll get an email when the e-Visa is approved. Print it or save it; airlines and immigration may ask to see it.

howToApply.step: Travel and fill in the TDAC
howToApply.detail: Submit the Thailand Digital Arrival Card within 3 days before arrival. Enter Thailand before the visa's 'enter before' date.

bestFor: Travellers who used to rely on the 60-day exemption
notFor: Remote work or long stays of 6 months or more (look at the DTV)
Business meetings or any work (use a Non-Immigrant B visa)
Short trips under 30 days if your passport is visa-exempt
commonMistakes: Applying too early. The visa's 3-month validity starts on the day it's issued, not the day you arrive.
Applying through the wrong embassy. You must apply where you legally live, not where you're passing through.
Uploading a bank statement with no name or date on it.
Believing the visa gives 90 days on arrival. You get 60 days; the extra 30 need an extension at immigration.
Using third-party 'visa agent' sites that look official. The only official site is thaievisa.go.th.
Letting a METV expire while abroad, expecting to re-enter on it.

faqs.q: How long can I stay on a Thai tourist visa?
faqs.a: Up to 60 days per entry. You can then apply once for a 30-day extension at an immigration office in Thailand for 1,900 THB, so up to 90 days in total per entry.

faqs.q: Is the multiple-entry tourist visa (METV) discontinued?
faqs.a: No. The METV still exists: it is valid for 6 months and allows up to 60 days per entry. Not every embassy offers it through the e-Visa system, and it usually asks for more financial evidence than the single-entry visa, so check your embassy's page.

faqs.q: Do I need a tourist visa if my passport is visa-exempt?
faqs.a: Only if you want to stay longer than your exemption allows. Since 15 September 2026 most visa-exempt travellers get 30 days, extendable by 30. If you want 60 days from the start, or up to 90 days, a tourist visa is the cleaner option.

faqs.q: Can I apply for the tourist visa at the airport or while I'm in another country?
faqs.a: No. You apply online before travelling, through the Thai embassy covering the country where you live. If you're a temporary visitor somewhere else, that embassy may refuse your application.

faqs.q: How much money do I need to show?
faqs.a: At least 20,000 THB per person or 40,000 THB per family for a single-entry visa. How many months of statements you need varies by embassy, and the METV asks for more.

faqs.q: Can I work remotely on a tourist visa?
faqs.a: No. Tourist visas don't allow any work. The Destination Thailand Visa (DTV) is the visa designed for remote workers.
